findings.reason: a coordinator reading the plan's forward state would dispatch §2 again and would not see the §6 repair node at all, so the plan must resolve `f-wicd-001` and open a followup naming that repair node.
findings.text: the plan's only followup `f-wicd-001` is still `data-status="open"` with `data-recommends-skill="/reckon-build work-is-checked-against-its-domain §2"` and the prompt `/reckon-build work-is-checked-against-its-domain §2`, and its body still reads "§2 and §3 can start at once … §7 replays the cases once the rest land", while §2, §3, §4, §5, §8, §9 and §10 are all declared `done` and §6 is half landed — so the chain that is supposed to carry the next one-line invocation instead names a section that is already built, and the §6 landing comment's own "a repair node follows" is carried nowhere

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — §6's cited `reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py`, `reckon/crew/prescription.py`, `reckon/crew/node.py` and `reckon/crew/domain_rules.py` all exist with the named symbols (`judge_prescribed` at prescription.py:130, `TaskNode.inputs`/`compares_with` at node.py:756-757, `rules_for` at domain_rules.py:160, `admission_domain_findings` at dispatch_admission.py:1873), `rules_for` does match `model_paths` against write paths (domain_rules.py:198-204), the cited purity docstring is real (prescription.py:29-35), and the landing comment's `#s6-inputs` anchor resolves in the evidence archive.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §6's done-when names a declared negative control ("A project that declares no `model_paths` is never linted"), a positive arm for each check, and a regression clause for the moved decision (`judge_prescribed` still judges a synthesised node with no repository).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §6's landing record sits at `docs/evidence/archive/work-is-checked-against-its-domain-landed.html`, a committed durable path, not a scratchpad or node-local temporary.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `inputs`, `compares_with` and `none-exists` are mechanism names; the changed units carry no plan label, ticket number or version tag, and the landing comment's "refuses rather than warns" is a state record rather than changelog prose in code.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — §6's root cause matches the §1 evidence (a fit started on constants nobody holds; two node rounds that no one asked "is there a measurement of this?"), the mechanism produces its done-when, and the mechanism runs on a production path: `_require_write_paths_in_authority` (dispatch_admission.py:1918-1932) is called from `reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:820` and its `admission_findings` are merged into the verdict by `_sandbox_reachability` (dispatch_admission.py:1951), so the checks are not test-only.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §6 carries one deliverable, a node declaring its prerequisites at admission; the two fields `inputs` and `compares_with` are two aspects of that one declaration and the section's node landed both.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §6's depends-on `work-is-checked-against-its-domain#s3` resolves and is correct, but the plan's own forward wiring is dead: its sole followup `f-wicd-001` still carries §2's build invocation while §2 is declared `done`.
